name: Webex Events
description: Webex Events, formerly Socio, is an event-management platform for virtual, hybrid, and in-person events with event apps, registration, onsite tools, streaming, exhibitors, sponsors, engagement, lead retrieval, and analytics.
agentUseSummary: Webex Events cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because Cisco gates the GraphQL endpoint, schema, authentication contract, and API documentation behind customer API entitlement and does not publish a distributable public contract Relay can implement safely.

blocked.label: Connect Webex Events
blocked.description: Relay cannot accept a Webex Events API key before Cisco supplies a current endpoint, header, schema, versioning, permission, and rate-limit contract that Relay is authorized to implement.

blocked.label: Use the gated GraphQL API
blocked.description: The public provider guidance confirms a GraphQL API but directs entitled customers to documentation inside the private organization API dashboard; Relay does not guess operations or mount an undocumented broad schema.

blocked.label: Automate the private platform
blocked.description: Relay does not sign in to the organizer platform, scrape private API documentation, reuse browser sessions, automate the API dashboard, or capture one-time API keys.

blocked.label: Substitute Webex Meetings or Compliance Events
blocked.description: Webex Meetings webinars and the Webex compliance Events API are separate provider contracts and are not presented as the Webex Events (formerly Socio) event-management API.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Cisco grants Relay a current distributable Webex Events API contract with sufficient documentation and test entitlement.

runtimeSupport.description: No safely implementable public Webex Events GraphQL contract is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No safely implementable public Webex Events GraphQL contract is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Cisco confirms that Webex Events has a metered GraphQL API and customer-created API keys, but API access is limited to entitled customers and the endpoint, schema, authentication headers, version contract, permissions, and rate limits are exposed only inside the private organization API dashboard.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request a key or show Connect. Reconsider after Cisco grants Relay a Webex Events API sandbox or entitled customer contract and permits access to current distributable documentation sufficient to pin typed, bounded, least-privilege operations.

evidence.supports: Cisco confirms a metered GraphQL API, API keys created by organization admins, automatic access for activated Suite EA customers, paid/support-gated access for others, and documentation available through the entitled organization API dashboard.
Cisco publishes broad Webex Events service allowlist domains, including wildcard API infrastructure, but not a stable public GraphQL endpoint or schema suitable for a pinned Relay connector.
Cisco describes Webex Events as a live SaaS event platform and directs customers to its trust materials; the blocker is gated integration documentation rather than product discontinuation.
